_meta.policy: Voltage-drop DESIGN TARGETS for solar and battery circuits. These are performance and economics choices, NOT safety limits and NOT code requirements. They are pre-filled starting points that the user can and should change.
_meta.whyNotSealed: The sealed tables in data-golden.json hold published electrical FACTS (ampacities, conductor areas, volume allowances) where a wrong digit is dangerous. These numbers are design preferences: a wrong one costs yield or copper, not safety. They live here, version-controlled and test-protected, so a change is visible in a diff — but they deliberately do NOT claim the authority of a sealed code table.
_meta.sourcingStatus: UNSOURCED. Each value below is a commonly used starting point, not a figure traced to a standard. No page asserts that any standard requires them, and the UI labels them as starting points. Tracing them to citable sources (or replacing them with equipment-manufacturer guidance) is outstanding work — until then the honest presentation is 'starting point, set your own'.

scenarios.reason: On a panel circuit, voltage drop is lost yield for the life of the system. A tighter target than a branch circuit is normal because the loss is continuous rather than occasional.
Drop between the charge controller and the battery makes the controller read a lower battery voltage than the real one, which can end a charge cycle early and leave the bank undercharged.

This is the tightest target of the three. Drop here is both lost power and lost low-voltage-cutout margin: the inverter sees battery voltage minus the cable drop, so a sagging cable can shut it down while the bank still holds charge.
